subject: ela
intro: This worksheet covers the whole Key Ideas and Details cluster for informational text: using details and examples to explain a text and draw inferences (4.RI.A.1), finding the main idea and how details support it, plus summarizing (4.RI.A.2), and explaining events, procedures, and ideas including what happened and why (4.RI.A.3). Items are grouped by standard and get harder toward the end of each group.

items.prompt:
Read the passage.

A hummingbird is one of the smallest birds in the world. It can beat its wings so fast that they become a blur. It is even able to fly backward, which almost no other bird can do.

What can a hummingbird do that almost no other bird can do? Use a detail from the text.
items.answer: A hummingbird can fly backward, which almost no other bird can do. The text says it is "able to fly backward."

steps: The question asks for a stated detail.
The text says the hummingbird is "able to fly backward, which almost no other bird can do."
I quote that detail.

items.prompt:
Read the passage.

The rings inside a tree trunk can tell its age. Each year the tree grows one new ring. In a rainy year the ring is wide, and in a dry year the ring is thin.

How can you tell the age of a tree, according to the text?
items.answer: You can tell a tree's age by counting the rings inside its trunk, because the tree grows one new ring each year. The text says, "Each year the tree grows one new ring."

steps: The question asks how to find a tree's age.
The text says the tree "grows one new ring" each year.
So counting the rings gives the age.

items.prompt:
Read the passage.

When the weather turns cold, a snowshoe hare grows a new coat of white fur. In summer, its fur is brown to match the dirt and leaves. Hawks and foxes often pass right by without spotting it.

What can you infer is the purpose of the hare's changing fur? Use a detail to support your answer.
items.answer: I can infer the changing fur helps the hare hide from animals that hunt it. The text says its fur matches the snow or the ground, and that hawks and foxes "often pass right by without spotting it."

steps: The purpose is not stated directly, so I gather clues.
The white fur matches snow and the brown fur matches dirt and leaves.
Since hunters "pass right by without spotting it," the fur is for hiding.

items.prompt:
Read the passage.

Harriet Tubman escaped from slavery, but she did not stay safely away. Again and again, she secretly returned to lead other enslaved people to freedom in the North. She traveled at night and never lost a single person she guided.

What can you infer about Harriet Tubman from her actions? Support your answer with details.
items.answer: I can infer that Harriet Tubman was very brave and caring. Even after reaching safety, she "secretly returned to lead other enslaved people to freedom" and "never lost a single person she guided."

steps: The text does not label her with one word, so I infer from her actions.
She kept returning into danger to free others and never lost anyone.
This shows she was brave and cared about others.

items.prompt:
Read the passage.

Deep in a cave, it is always pitch black. A fish called the blind cavefish lives there. Over thousands of years, these fish lost their eyes completely, since eyes were of no use in the dark. Instead, they feel tiny movements in the water to find food and avoid walls.

Why do you think the cavefish lost their eyes? Use details from the text to explain your inference.
items.answer: I can infer the cavefish lost their eyes because eyes were useless in the pitch-black cave. The text says the cave is "always pitch black" and that "eyes were of no use in the dark," so the fish rely on feeling movements in the water instead.

steps: I combine clues to make an inference.
The cave is "always pitch black" and "eyes were of no use in the dark."
So the fish lost their eyes and now feel movements to survive.

items.prompt:
Read the passage.

Birds have many kinds of beaks. A hawk has a sharp, hooked beak for tearing meat. A hummingbird has a long, thin beak to sip nectar from flowers. A duck has a wide, flat beak to scoop food from the water.

What is the main idea of this passage?
items.answer: The main idea is that birds have many kinds of beaks that are shaped to fit the food they eat.

steps: Each sentence describes a different beak and its use.
The first sentence states the big point.
So the main idea is that birds have many kinds of beaks for their food.

items.prompt:
Read the passage.

Getting enough sleep helps you in school. When you sleep, your brain sorts and stores what you learned that day. A rested brain remembers facts better on a test. Sleep also helps you pay attention instead of feeling grumpy and tired.

Name one key detail that supports the main idea that sleep helps you in school.
items.answer: One supporting detail is that when you sleep, "your brain sorts and stores what you learned that day," which helps you remember better.

steps: The main idea is that sleep helps you in school.
I look for a detail that shows a benefit.
The brain sorting and storing what you learned is one supporting detail.

items.prompt:
Read the passage.

The first firefighters in America used bucket brigades. When a fire started, neighbors formed a long line from a well to the fire. They passed buckets of water from hand to hand up the line. Empty buckets were passed back down the other side to be filled again. Everyone had to help, or the fire would win.

Write a short summary of this passage.
items.answer: The first American firefighters used bucket brigades. Neighbors formed a line from a well to the fire, passed full buckets of water up the line and empty ones back down, and everyone had to help to put the fire out.

steps: The main idea is how early firefighters fought fires with bucket brigades.
The key details are the line of neighbors passing buckets up and back.
I retell these briefly in my own words.

items.prompt:
Read the passage.

Wetlands are lands that stay soaked with water, like marshes and swamps. They do important work. Their plants act like a giant sponge that soaks up floodwaters and protects nearby towns. They filter dirt and poisons out of the water, making it cleaner. They are also home to frogs, birds, and fish.

What is the main idea, and give two details that support it.
items.answer: The main idea is that wetlands do important work for people and animals. Two supporting details are that their plants "soak up floodwaters and protect nearby towns" and they "filter dirt and poisons out of the water."

steps: The big point is that wetlands do important work.
I look for details that show their value.
Soaking up floods and filtering water are two supporting details.

items.prompt:
Read the passage.

For most of history, people copied books slowly by hand, one at a time, so books were rare and costly. In the 1400s, Johannes Gutenberg built a printing press with movable letters. Now the same page could be printed over and over quickly. Books became cheap enough for ordinary people to own. As more people got books, more people learned to read, and new ideas spread across the world.

What is the main idea of this passage? Write a one-sentence main idea, then a short summary.
items.answer: Main idea: Gutenberg's printing press made books cheap and common, which helped more people read and spread new ideas. Summary: Before the printing press, books were copied slowly by hand and were rare and costly. In the 1400s, Gutenberg's press could print pages quickly, so books became cheap, more people learned to read, and new ideas spread across the world.

steps: The big point is that the printing press changed the world by making books common.
The key details are the slow hand-copying before, the fast press, and the spread of reading and ideas.
I state the main idea in one sentence and then summarize the key points.

items.prompt:
Read the passage.

Bubbles are made of a thin skin of soapy water with air trapped inside. When you blow gently through a wand, air pushes into the soapy film and stretches it out. The film wraps all the way around the air and pinches off into a round bubble.

Using the text, explain how a bubble forms.
items.answer: A bubble forms when you blow air into a thin skin of soapy water on the wand. The air stretches the soapy film out, and the film wraps around the air and pinches off into a round bubble.

steps: I follow how the bubble is made.
Air "pushes into the soapy film and stretches it out."
The film wraps around the air and pinches off as a bubble.

items.prompt:
Read the passage.

A cut on your skin heals in steps. First, the blood at the cut gets sticky and forms a scab that seals the opening. Under the scab, new skin slowly grows to fill the gap. When the new skin is ready, the scab dries up and falls off on its own.

Using the text, explain what happens under the scab while a cut heals.
items.answer: While a cut heals, new skin slowly grows under the scab to fill the gap. When that new skin is ready, the scab dries up and falls off on its own.

steps: I find what happens beneath the scab.
The text says "new skin slowly grows to fill the gap."
When it is ready, the scab falls off.

items.prompt:
Read the passage.

Why do we have day and night? The Earth is always spinning like a slow top. As it spins, one side faces the Sun and has daytime. At the same time, the other side is turned away from the Sun and has nighttime. It takes 24 hours for the Earth to spin all the way around once.

Using the text, explain why we have day and night.
items.answer: We have day and night because the Earth is always spinning. The side facing the Sun has daytime, while the side turned away from the Sun has nighttime, and it takes 24 hours to spin all the way around.

steps: I find the cause of day and night.
The Earth "is always spinning," so one side faces the Sun and one is turned away.
The facing side has day and the other has night.

items.prompt:
Read the passage.

In 1849, thousands of people rushed to California after gold was found there. They came by wagon and by ship, hoping to get rich quickly. Most did not find much gold, but so many people moved west that new towns sprang up almost overnight. Stores, hotels, and roads were built to serve the crowds.

Using the text, explain what happened after gold was found in California and why new towns appeared.
items.answer: After gold was found in California in 1849, thousands of people rushed there by wagon and ship hoping to get rich. New towns appeared almost overnight because so many people moved west that stores, hotels, and roads had to be built to serve the crowds.

steps: I find what happened after the gold was found.
"Thousands of people rushed to California," and so many moved west that "new towns sprang up."
The towns appeared to serve all the new people.

items.prompt:
Read the passage.

Why does the wind blow? The Sun does not heat every part of the Earth evenly. Warm air is lighter, so it rises up and leaves an empty space below. Cooler, heavier air then rushes in to fill that space. This moving air is what we feel as wind. Where the difference in heat is large, the wind blows strong.

Using the text, explain what causes wind and why some winds are stronger than others.
items.answer: Wind is caused because the Sun heats the Earth unevenly. Warm air is lighter and rises, leaving an empty space, and cooler, heavier air rushes in to fill it. This moving air is the wind. Winds are stronger where the difference in heat is large.

steps: I trace the cause of wind.
Uneven heating makes warm air rise and cool air rush in to replace it.
That moving air is wind, and a bigger heat difference makes stronger wind.
